title: Stride Payments - POC scoping: workload modeling
summary: POC scoping to define success criteria and traffic model for Stride's fraud-detection LLM assistant. Discussed QPS/concurrency, token distributions, latency SLOs, benchmark plan and timelines. Agreed next steps: Stride to share 10k sample prompts + traffic trace; Redwood to propose benchmark plan and preliminary GPU sizing and pricing; schedule 2 week pilot starting mid-August.
next_steps: Customer to send 10k sample prompt set and 7-day traffic trace (Jenna) - due 2026-07-29
Redwood to deliver benchmark plan + hardware recommendation (Priya) - due 2026-07-27
Schedule 60m benchmarking kickoff & demo (Alex) - schedule by 2026-07-24
Send security pack (SOC2 + KMS integration notes) and preliminary pricing (Marcus) - due 2026-07-26
action_items: Jenna Ortiz: export anonymized 7-day traffic logs and 10k prompts - 2026-07-29
Priya Nair: draft benchmark plan, synthetic workload config, and expected metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec) - 2026-07-27
Alex Park: schedule pilot kickoff meeting and invite stakeholders - 2026-07-24
Marcus Li: share HW sizing estimates (A100 vs H100) and rough cost model - 2026-07-26
transcript:
Header: 2026-07-22 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Marcus (SE), Mark (Stride Head ML), Jenna (Eng Mgr), Samir (SRE), Olivia (PM)

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, with me are Priya and Marcus on the engineering side. Quick agenda, want to cover your success criteria, traffic shape, and then scope the POC benchmarks and timeline.
00:18 Mark: Hey thanks, yes we want to understand if Redwood can hit our latency and cost targets for the fraud assistant, and what dedicated footprint we'd need.
00:28 Priya: Great, can you give rough numbers for QPS and concurrency, and typical input/output sizes? Even ranges help.
00:35 Jenna: Sure rough numbers, average QPS is about 8-12 during normal hours, spikes to ~160 QPS at peak events, we see concurrency around 40-60 for the assistant because we fan-out some checks in parallel.
00:50 Samir: To add, our current infra experiences bursty traffic - 95th percentile of request interarrival is spiky at promo pushes.
01:02 Marcus: Okay that's helpful. Do you have token distribution? median input tokens, and expected generated tokens?
01:09 Jenna: Inputs are short - median ~30-50 tokens; but outputs vary, most are shorter summaries ~80-150 tokens, about 15% of requests are detailed explanations going up to 500 tokens.
01:25 Olivia: Also some requests are streaming for real-time analyst UI, low tail latency matters.
01:33 Priya: Got it. For our sizing we'll model three buckets: short (<=100 output tokens) ~70% of traffic, medium (100-300) ~15%, long (>300) ~15%. Does that align?
01:43 Jenna: Yes that aligns with our telemetry.
01:48 Alex: Success criteria - what's non-negotiable? Latency p95 or p99, cost per 1M tokens, accuracy metrics?
01:57 Mark: p95 interactive latency under 600ms is our goal for analyst flows, for async scoring we can accept up to 2s. Cost-wise we want to keep inference cost growth <30% vs our current baseline. Accuracy is tracked by our internal evals; we'll share eval prompts but won't block POC on perfect accuracy.
02:14 Priya: Understood. For Redwood hosted vs dedicated, tradeoffs are predictable throughput and data isolation. Are you leaning towards Private/VPC or dedicated reserved?
02:24 Mark: Data residency and logs are sensitive - we'd prefer dedicated reserved for initial POC but open to private if required for compliance.
02:33 Alex: Ok we'll note dedicated as primary. Security: SOC2, RBAC, KMS for encryption at rest, and VPC peering were listed in your RFP?
02:42 Jenna: Yes SAML SSO and KMS are must-haves. Also need audit log retention.
02:49 Marcus: Redwood supports KMS integration and audit logs; we'll include the security pack.
02:54 Alex: Let's talk benchmarks. Priya, could you outline recommended benchmark steps?
03:00 Priya: Sure. Step 1: ingest your 10k anonymized prompts and a 7-day traffic trace as replay for arrival rates. Step 2: synthetic load with three buckets matching token distribution; ramp to 1.2x observed peak to validate headroom. Step 3: measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll run both host-mode (shared) and dedicated-mode runs, and for dedicated we will test on A100 80GB and H100-ish configs if available. We'll also do KV/prefix cache experiments for repeated prefixes.
03:41 Jenna: Sounds good. How long does the benchmark take?
03:44 Priya: A full suite about 3-6 hours per configuration; quick sanity run in 60-90 minutes. We'll aim to do a quick run first then a longer run for final numbers.
03:54 Mark: For the POC timeline, we have legal review too - how long till we can start?
03:59 Alex: If you share artifacts this week we can start bench planning next week. Proposed pilot window: two weeks of reserved capacity for deeper testing, target mid-August start (around 2026-08-12).
04:12 Samir: On networking, we'll need VPC peering + allowlist. Also curious about egress restrictions for PII - will calls touch Redwood logs?
04:22 Marcus: We can run with logs disabled and push logs to your S3; for Private deployments there's no egress outside your VPC. We'll detail options in the security doc.
04:33 Priya: For hardware sizing preliminary estimate: based on 160 QPS peak and token distribution, short responses dominate, we'd estimate 2-4 H100-class GPUs for dedicated to meet p95 <600ms, depending on model choice and quantization. If you use a smaller model (quantized 4-bit) we might get away with 2 GPUs.
04:56 Jenna: Do you have per-GPU throughput numbers?
04:59 Priya: Approx numbers: with an LLM similar to the curated open model we proposed, a single H100 could sustain ~80-120 QPS for short-response heavy workloads with batching and KV cache; A100 is slightly lower. We'll provide more precise figures after bench.
05:13 Mark: Pricing expectations? We need a ballpark to get approvals.
05:18 Alex: We'll share a preliminary cost model - for dedicated it's an estimate of reserved GPU + per-token egress. Roughly expect dedicated costs in tens of thousands per month for the footprint we described, but we'll provide a detailed proposal.
05:31 Jenna: Good. Bench metrics - what are the pass/fail thresholds?
05:34 Priya: We'll propose pass thresholds: p95 latency <=600ms for interactive flows, p99 <=1.5s; throughput to sustain 1.2x peak without queue growth; GPU utilization in healthy range (50-90%); and cost per 1M tokens within your target threshold.
05:51 Mark: Sounds reasonable. Also want to include tail latency checks during spikes and cold-start behavior for cached vs uncached.
05:59 Priya: We'll include cold-start scenarios.
06:02 Alex: On deliverables, Redwood will provide: benchmark plan, hardware recommendation, security pack, and a demo run report. Any other docs?
06:10 Olivia: Please include sample SDK calls and retry/backoff guidance for our backend engineers.
06:15 Marcus: We'll include an integration guide and sample SDK snippets.
06:19 Jenna: For POC success, if we meet latency and controls and cost is acceptable then we proceed to a longer dedicated contract.
06:27 Mark: Timeline and approvals - legal and procurement typically need two weeks, so our mid-August pilot start is optimistic but doable.
06:35 Alex: Great. Any competitive concerns? Are you evaluating Anthropic or in-house options?
06:40 Mark: We're running internal experiments but Anthropic and OpenAI are in the mix. Main decision factors are latency/cost and the ease of rolling to dedicated/private.
06:50 Priya: Noted. We'll surface cost/lifecycle differences in the proposal.
06:55 Alex: Ok recap - Jenna sends sample prompts and trace by 7/29, Priya shares benchmark plan by 7/27, Marcus shares pricing and HW by 7/26, Alex schedules pilot kickoff by 7/24, Redwood sends security pack and SDK examples.
07:12 Jenna: I've got all that noted, will coordinate with legal.
07:17 Samir: One question - when you run the synthetic load, can we observe the runs in real-time?
07:22 Marcus: Yes we'll give you live dashboards (latency, GPU util, tokens/sec) and exportable CSVs.
07:29 Mark: Great. Any blockers?
07:32 Jenna: None from engineering aside from legal.
07:35 Alex: Thanks everyone, will follow up with calendar invites and artifacts.
07:39 (end)

Notes: transcript contains minor auto-transcription errors (names, acronyms occasionally mis-typed), speaker turns sometimes compressed. References: security pack link (redwood.com/security-pack) and benchmark sheet (redwood.com/benchmarks/stride-proposal) - placeholders, not real downloads.
notes: Customer prefers dedicated reserved capacity for initial POC due to data sensitivity.
Token distribution heavily short-output dominated; caching/prefix reuse likely to yield cost savings.
Recommended pilot: 2-week reserved capacity + 1 week planning/bench prep.
